contents.title: Quiz Diagnostic 1ere Anglais - Serie 39
contents.subject: Anglais
contents.description: Diagnostic Anglais 1ere : La description et l'analyse à l'écrit

questions.question: Which sentence is an ANALYSIS rather than just a description?
choices: There is a woman standing near a window.
The woman is wearing a red dress.
The woman's isolated posture near the window suggests she feels lonely or disconnected from the world outside.
The window is large and lets in a lot of light.

questions.question: When describing an image, it is good practice to start with the general scene before moving to specific details.
Transforme cette description en analyse : 'The factory emits a lot of smoke into the sky.'
Which expression is most appropriate to introduce an interpretation in an analytical text?
In a descriptive piece, using a variety of adjectives and sensory details (sight, sound, smell) makes the writing more vivid and engaging.
Décris et analyse brièvement cette situation en 2 phrases : un enfant seul dans une salle de classe vide, la tête baissée sur son bureau.
Which verb best completes an analytical sentence about a photograph? 'The image ___ the contrast between wealth and poverty.'
A good analytical paragraph about a document should only focus on what is explicitly visible or written, never on what is implied.

exercisenotion.notion: Décrire une image ou une scène
exercisenotion.description: Pour décrire une image en anglais : commencer par le contexte général (In this picture, we can see...), puis décrire les éléments principaux (In the foreground/background/centre...), les personnages (appearance, actions), l'atmosphère (The image conveys..., The mood seems...). Utiliser le present simple pour les descriptions.

exercisenotion.notion: Analyser un document : texte ou image
exercisenotion.description: L'analyse va au-delà de la description : elle interprète, cherche le sens profond, identifie les intentions de l'auteur. Formules utiles : This suggests that... / This implies... / The author seems to argue... / One can infer that... / This is significant because... / The use of [X] highlights [Y].

Vocabulaire de description : depicts, portrays, illustrates, shows, features, presents, focuses on, centres on. Vocabulaire d'analyse : emphasises, conveys, implies, suggests, reveals, challenges, critiques, underlines, demonstrates, reflects. Connecteurs : furthermore, in addition, as a result, consequently, in contrast, similarly, notably.
